title: Reject fixture attached to F.2, a section that contains no prohibition at all
detail: VERIFIED: the full text of F.2 (docs/VAMS-LRM/annex-f-resolution.html, before F.2.1) contains no 'shall not', no 'is an error', no 'illegal' — it is pure descriptive text about parent/child net segments and traversal order. The fixture nevertheless carries `//! reject module instantiation is not supported` on `child u(sig);`, which is legal Verilog-AMS (A.4.1 module_instantiation, ch6). Its own header says 'DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance'. The fact it actually pins is VerA's E0204, already pinned canonically by tests/fixtures/ch06_hierarchy/module_instantiation_unsupported.va, so deleting loses no requirement. The .expected-error.txt sidecar goes with it: README.md line 3 says 'No sidecar files', and tests/torture.zig is the only runner wired into build.zig (the sidecar-reading tests/conformance.zig has no build step), so the sidecar is dead bytes that only re-state the substring.
expected: A conforming compiler elaborates `child u(sig)` and resolves sig; it emits no diagnostic. Nothing in F.2 can be violated by this source.

title: Second copy of the same non-LRM rejection, occupying the F.2.1 slot in COVERAGE.md
detail: VERIFIED: identical shape to F-01 — quotes five F.2.1 rules verbatim in comments, then pins `//! reject module instantiation is not supported` on `analog_leaf a(sig); digital_leaf d(sig);`. That topology is exactly the one F.2.1 step 4 is about, and the fixture stops before any of it: no rule in the header is exercised. A CONFORMING compiler must accept this file, so it FAILS the fixture while VerA passes it — the definition of anti-conformant. Same E0204 duplicate as F-01. Sidecar deleted with it.
expected: A conforming compiler resolves sig: children are one analog and one digital, so per F.2.1 step 4a 'any others shall be considered analog', and it inserts an interface element at this level. No diagnostic.

title: Third copy of the E0204 rejection, and F.2.2 is by its own text not selectable from source
detail: VERIFIED: same DEBT header, same `//! reject module instantiation is not supported`, same legal source. Beyond the inversion, F.2.2 states 'The selection of this algorithm instead of the default shall be controlled by a simulator option' — no Verilog-AMS source construct chooses it, so NO .va file can ever distinguish F.2.2 from F.2.1. This fixture cannot be repaired into a conformance test; it can only be deleted and the reason recorded (F-10). Sidecar deleted with it. After F-01..F-04 the chapter has zero .expected-error.txt files, closing the README 'No sidecar files' violation for this directory.
expected: No source-level verdict exists for F.2.2. A conforming compiler running the default algorithm and one running the alternate algorithm both accept this file.

title: Demands a PARSE ERROR on the construct the LRM prints as its own example
detail: VERIFIED against two places in the LRM. F.2.1 step 3 and F.2.2 step 3: 'For example, electrical top.middle.bottom.sig; overrides any discipline which may be declared for sig in the module where sig was declared.' And ch3-datatypes.html 3.10 'Discipline precedence' prints `module example1; electrical example2.net; endmodule` as the HIGHEST-precedence legal form. The fixture pins ``//! reject expected `;` `` on exactly that syntax. It is not merely inverted: it also contains no in-context declaration to override, so even read charitably it tests the opposite of the rule it cites. Its LRM content is not lost — F-07 re-uses the same syntax pointing the right way, as a reject+xfail on the conflicting-OOC prohibition.
expected: A conforming compiler parses `electrical top.middle.bottom.sig;` and applies it as an out-of-context declaration that overrides the in-context one (3.10 precedence order 1 over order 2).

title: CHECK with 1e-15 absolute tolerance on a bit-exact read-back; CHECKX is the correct macro
detail: VERIFIED, and BOTH LITERALS ARE CORRECT — no wrong number exists in this chapter. Annex F is an algorithm annex ('provides a possible algorithm') and defines no numeric quantity, so there is nothing here to get wrong. The two 0.7 wants are read-backs of the `//! bias` directive: src/backend/tb.zig emits `x[ix("...")] = 0.7;` as a hard store into the unknown vector, and the generated runner has no Newton solve, so `got` is a bit-exact load of the same double (0x1.6666666666666p-1) and the difference is exactly 0.0. The 1e-15 absolute slack is ~9 ulp at 0.7 with no source, and README's own table reserves CHECK for 'values near zero'. Change both call sites to `CHECKX(NAME, GOT, WANT)` (drop the tolerance argument). Do NOT change the 0.7 values.
expected: `CHECKX("...", V(p), 0.7);` and `CHECKX("...", Fpot(sig), 0.7);` — ok=1 by exact equality.

title: The one correctly-pointed fixture in the chapter is a permanent red: no //! lrm, no //! xfail
detail: VERIFIED BY RUNNING `zig build torture -- annex_f_resolution`: 'FAIL conflicting_declarations.va: expected a diagnostic, but it compiled cleanly'. The fixture is right and VerA is wrong — grep of src/diag_code.zig shows no conflicting-discipline-declaration diagnostic exists — which is precisely the case README's XFAIL verdict is for. Add three lines: `//! lrm F.2.1`, `//! lrm 3.10`, and `//! xfail VerA has no conflicting-discipline diagnostic; two declarations for one net are accepted silently`. XPASS is safe here: VerA emits ZERO diagnostics on this file, so the `DiagnosticsReported` reject substring cannot be satisfied accidentally, and the day VerA does diagnose it the xfail line correctly hard-FAILs as XPASS. ALSO fold in the 'compatible or not' clarification the negatives and uncovered lenses asked for as a separate fixture: annex_f_a and annex_f_b are both natureless with `domain continuous`, and 3.11.1's Natureless Discipline Rule makes them COMPATIBLE with each other — so this file already IS the 'regardless of whether the disciplines are compatible or not' case. One prose line saying that is the whole fix; no second fixture is needed.
expected: Verdict flips from FAIL to XFAIL with a printed reason and §F.2.1 §3.10 cites; --strict still fails on it so the gap is not forgotten.

title: No fixture for conflicting OUT-OF-CONTEXT declarations — the other half of the step-3 prohibition
detail: VERIFIED uncovered: the step-3 sentence prohibits 'more than one conflicting in-context discipline declaration OR more than one conflicting out-of-context discipline declaration'. conflicting_declarations.va covers only the in-context half; grep of the directory finds no dotted-path declaration outside the (deleted) out_of_context_unsupported.va. Write two conflicting OOM declarations for one segment, e.g. `module f_ooc_conflict; annex_f_a top.child.sig; annex_f_b top.child.sig; endmodule`, with `//! lrm F.2.1`, `//! lrm 3.10` and `//! xfail`. AUTHOR TRAP, do not miss it: VerA currently emits a PARSE error ('expected `;`') on dotted declarations, so the reject line must NOT be the generic `DiagnosticsReported` — that would MATCH the parse error, XPASS, and hard-FAIL. Use a substring specific to the rule that does not exist yet, e.g. `//! reject conflicting discipline declaration`.
expected: A conforming compiler parses both declarations and rejects the file with a conflicting-declaration error. VerA stops at the parser, so the verdict is XFAIL until both the dotted-path parse and the conflict check land.

title: The annex's only other prohibition — unknown discipline WITH a mixed-port connection is an error — has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED uncovered: 'Otherwise the discipline is unknown. This is legal provided the net has no mixed-port connections... Otherwise this is an error.' Nothing in the chapter reaches it. Write a net left undeclared, resolving to no discipline, connected through a port to a segment of the other domain; add `//! lrm F.2.1` and `//! xfail`. Same XPASS trap as F-07: VerA will emit E0204 (module instantiation) long before resolution, so the reject substring must be rule-specific (e.g. `mixed-port`), never `DiagnosticsReported` and never the E0204 text. SCOPE NOTE: the negatives lens listed this prohibition three times (F.2.1 4.b, F.2.2 4.b, F.2.2 5.b). The F.2.2 pair is the SAME sentence in an algorithm that 'shall be controlled by a simulator option', so no source fixture can distinguish them — one fixture is the complete coverage available, and F-10 records why.
expected: A conforming compiler rejects the file with an unresolved-discipline/mixed-port error. VerA stops at E0204, so XFAIL.

title: Asserts nothing, cannot run, and its declared discipline is unused — yet it is credited in COVERAGE.md
detail: VERIFIED BY RUNNING: 'CANNOT RUN discrete_discipline.va: the device contract refuses this module — no port list'. Seven lines: it declares `annex_f_discrete` and then never uses it; the module `annex_f_discrete_marker` has no port list and declares `electrical p` (not the discrete discipline); there is no `//! reject`, no `//! lrm` and no CHECK, so it is unasserted AND refused — two --strict failures for one file. It cannot be repaired into an Annex F test: Annex F is about UNDECLARED nets, and 3.6.3 forbids a discrete net in analog behavioral code, so a single flat module has nothing to say. `domain discrete` parsing is already covered by ch07_mixed_signal/discrete_discipline.va, annex_d_standard_definitions/discrete_disciplines.va, annex_d/literal_logic_discipline.va and annex_c_analog_subset/07. Delete and drop the sF-1 credit in COVERAGE.md.
expected: Nothing — the file makes no claim. Deleting it removes one CANNOT RUN and one unasserted from the suite.

title: State the annex as structurally unreachable instead of selling VerA snapshots as coverage
detail: After F-01..F-04 and F-09, three .va files remain and the current table is wrong in every row: sF-1 credits a deleted file, sF-2 and sF-2-2 credit deleted files, sF-2-1 credits two deleted files. Rewrite it to say the true thing, which the audit establishes: Annex F is a hierarchy-elaboration algorithm over undeclared interconnect, VerA compiles ONE flat module (E0204 'module instantiation is not supported', src/diag_code.zig:679), so ~17 of the annex's ~21 rules are unreachable by construction, not merely untested. Name them in one list so the gap is greppable: continuous-over-discrete precedence and continuous passed up the hierarchy (F.2); parent/child orientation, post-order and top-down traversal (F.2); in-context declaration applying to ALL instances, out-of-context override, digital-behavioral-code classification, F.2.1 4a all-children-digital-else-ANALOG vs F.2.2 4a all-others-still-UNKNOWN (the sole difference between the two algorithms), the domain-filtered candidate list, the empty-list `default_discipline branch, the single-discipline branch, the resolveto branch, unknown-is-legal-without-mixed-ports, and F.2.2 step 5's top-down re-visit. Delete the 'snapshot the missing diagnostic' framing. Two further notes to record: (1) F.2.2 is selected by a simulator option, so it is unreachable even for a full elaborator driven from source; (2) extending `//! xfail` to run fixtures (README lines 194-195 limit it to `//! reject`) was considered as a way to write the positive rules and is NOT proposed here — it would produce ~17 fixtures that all XFAIL on the one E0204 already pinned by ch06_hierarchy/module_instantiation_unsupported.va. OUT OF SCOPE but worth forwarding: the uncovered lens is right that `default_discipline's actual effect is untested suite-wide — ch10_directives/01,02,24 and annex_c/09 all declare their nets explicitly and each header admits the directive is a no-op there. That belongs in ch10's work order.
expected: A reader can tell from COVERAGE.md alone which Annex F sentences have a fixture, which are gaps with a named blocker, and which no .va file can ever reach.

title: The chapter's two live fixtures carry no //! lrm cite, and what they pin is not Annex F
detail: VERIFIED: grep of `//!` in the directory shows not one `//! lrm` line in the whole chapter, so `--coverage` reports Annex F as cited by nothing. Both files also pin 3.6.2.2/3.5 access-function binding on an explicitly DECLARED net — Annex F is about UNDECLARED nets, so neither exercises an Annex F sentence. Cheapest honest fix is cites, not a move: add `//! lrm 3.6.2.2` (+ `//! lrm 3.6.3`) to continuous_discipline.va and `//! lrm 3.10` (+ `//! lrm 3.6.2.2`) to in_context_declaration.va — 3.10 precedence order 2, 'the local declaration of the net in the module to which it belongs', is genuinely what in_context_declaration.va demonstrates. Combine with F-05, same two files, one commit.
expected: `zig build torture -- --coverage` attributes these two fixtures to the clauses they actually pin, and Annex F stops claiming them.
